description: Step 3 of /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.183.html, redefined by fz-sc8.183.2, which already made an unread field a bounds check. What is left: a string-literal segment such as <<"\"", r :: binary>> is a binary-typed field of literal size tested with Region::Equal(Const(Utf8Binary)). Each clause tried builds a one-byte view (fz_bs_read_binary_ref), allocates the constant (Prim::ConstBitstring -> fz_alloc_bitstring_const) and calls generic equality (fz_value_eq_ref). The integer form <<34, r :: binary>> is a raw compare and allocates nothing. Measured: lit.fz 4 allocations per step against int.fz 1 (after .183.2); rewriting lib/json.fz's 37 literal patterns as integers took the built distiller from 4.26 s to 3.06 s on 16,000 lines (release), same output. Fix: where the pattern is built, a literal binary segment becomes one integer-8 field per byte, each with an integer equality test, so it shares the decision tree with integer-literal clauses and needs no new primitive. Signal: lit.fz equals int.fz in allocations per step on interp, run and build; json_decode_cost goldens fall; distiller timing re-measured.
title: A string literal in a binary pattern is tested as its bytes
